title: Cross-language mock-proxy + VCR-style contract tests for streaming & retry semantics
creator: Anika Rao
description:
Goal: Build a cross-language test harness that validates Redwood API streaming and retry behavior across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. Instead of language-specific naive replay fixtures, this ticket implements a mock-proxy + canonicalization layer that captures real traffic with VCR-style cassettes, normalizes volatile fields, and asserts protocol-level contracts: chunk boundaries, SSE/event ordering, Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding semantics, reconnect/resume flows, and retry-idempotency.

Scope:
- Implement a lightweight HTTP mock-proxy that can operate in two modes: capture (record to cassettes) and playback (serve deterministic, normalized event streams).
- Provide per-language client adapters/examples that show how the Python async iterator, TS ReadableStream/EventSource, and Go io.Reader approaches consume the playback stream deterministically.
- Add cassette canonicalization rules (strip ephemeral auth headers, normalize timestamps, collapse small timing jitter, canonicalize request ids) and a policy for tolerated reordering when appropriate.
- Expand CI to run contract suites for all three SDKs in a matrix: capture mode run occasionally against staging, playback mode run on every PR.
- Add assertions for retry behavior: verify that client retry hooks fire exactly N times for simulated transient 5xxs, verify that idempotency/retry tokens are passed or regenerated according to client config, and verify that partial streaming responses are resumed correctly when server sends reconnect markers.

Why a proxy vs a recorder embedded in each SDK: the proxy centralizes capture/playback logic and ensures identical cassettes are consumable by all SDKs. This avoids subtle language-level differences in chunking when capturing from each SDK directly. The proxy also allows sanitization and canonicalization in one place and simplifies cassette review during incidents.
acceptance_criteria: A mock-proxy binary/container image that can run in capture and playback modes and is included in dev tooling
Canonicalization rules document checked in (confluence + repo README) describing fields stripped/normalized
At least 6 representative cassettes captured from staging showing streaming, partial failures, reconnects, and retry scenarios
Three SDK examples (python/ts/go) consuming playback cassettes with deterministic outputs checked into tests/fixtures
CI job matrix runs playback-mode contract tests on every PR and fails on contract regressions
Retry semantics assertions included: expected retry count, idempotency token behavior, and resume correctness
Runbook snippet for converting a live incident trace into a cassette for postmortem included in the repo
notes: 2026-01-20 - Triage: flagged as P1 after recent flaky streaming regressions in production; customer impact classified as medium
2026-01-25 - Design: decided on proxy-based approach to produce SDK-agnostic cassettes; trade-offs discussed: single source of truth vs additional infra component to maintain
2026-01-28 - Spike complete: prototype proxy (Go) streams captured chunk boundaries as explicit event frames; proof-of-concept cassette loaded by Python async iterator and TS EventSource shim

2026-02-02 - Review feedback from SDK leads (Lara Ortiz, Priyanka Mehta): add canonicalization for ephemeral request IDs and also normalize whitespace in multi-line structured outputs to avoid brittle diffs
2026-02-05 - Implementation: added playback speed throttling option to simulate backpressure and a 'fuzz' toggle to introduce small jitter for robustness tests
2026-02-08 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1208 - includes proxy server + python/ts/go example adapters; requesting review from eng-infra and SDK owners

2026-02-09 - Security note: cassette capture can include sensitive headers; added default sanitizer to remove Authorization and X-Amz-* headers. Filed follow-up to add KMS-encrypted cassette storage for enterprise customers
2026-02-10 - Next: finalize CI config, add more edge-case cassettes (interleaved multi-stream responses), and schedule cross-SDK runathon to validate flaky cases
